meta.why: Removed from the country file: web-checked and confirmed not to be published documents — synthesised meta/framing nodes, geographic areas, industries, projects, institutions. Banned by data spec 2b/2c. Kept here in full so nothing is lost.

reports.title: Cross-Strait / Chinese-connections architecture (meta-node)
reports.publisher: Derived from MAC, Investment Commission, ECFA offices, Customs and related sources
reports.description: Meta-node that binds ECFA (legal + early-harvest execution), MAC Cross-Strait Economic Statistics, outbound and inbound investment series, trade-share indicators, people-exchange statistics and residual financial linkages into a coherent cross-strait cluster. Explicitly positioned as the commercial and historical counterpart (and partial opposite) to the US–Taiwan economic-security and semiconductor-sovereignty architecture.
reports._notes: Integrating node designed so the force layout can treat ‘Chinese commercial connections’ as a high-mass object that pulls against the chips–sovereignty and US economic-security clusters. Captures both residual interdependence and the measured decoupling.
_referenced_by: All detailed cross-strait nodes in this batch
US–Taiwan ART / investment MOU / export-control nodes (Batch 8)
Semiconductor supply-chain and trade statistics that still contain Mainland intermediate-goods flows
National accounts, BOP and economic-security assessments

reports.title: USA–Taiwan–China economic-security triangle (meta-node)
reports.publisher: Derived from AIT–TECRO instruments, MAC, MOEA, US Commerce / USTR, and related official series
reports.description: Integrating meta-node that situates Taiwan’s semiconductor and trade statistics inside the triangular relationship with the United States (deepening economic-security alignment, reshoring, preferential trade) and Mainland China (residual commercial interdependence, declining relative dependence, strategic competition). Designed so the force layout can treat the three poles as a single high-mass geometric object.
reports._notes: Highest-level relational node. Pulls the previously separate US-security, Chinese-commercial and Taiwan-chip clusters into an explicit triangle.
_referenced_by: US–Taiwan ART / investment MOU / export-control nodes (Batch 8)
Semiconductor production, science-park and advanced-capacity nodes (Batches 7–8)
Military / navy and US FMS nodes (Batch 9)

reports.title: ‘Silicon shield’ / strategic semiconductor concentration logic
reports.publisher: Derived from official Taiwan and US policy language, National Defense Report, and industrial statistics
reports.description: Recurring strategic concept that Taiwan’s dominant share of advanced semiconductor manufacturing capacity functions as an asymmetric deterrent and as a source of interdependence with the United States and global technology economies. Continuously referenced in defence, industrial and diplomatic documents.
reports._notes: Conceptual but heavily cited node that explains why the semiconductor cluster carries geopolitical weight inside the triangle.
_referenced_by: National Defense Report and economic-security documents

reports.title: US import share shift — Taiwan vs China (goods trade)
reports.publisher: US Census / Commerce data as reported and analysed in Taiwan official and statistical releases
reports.description: Statistical observation that, under recent tariff and demand conditions, US goods imports from Taiwan have at times exceeded those from China, while Taiwan’s export orientation has shifted markedly toward the United States (US share of Taiwan exports rising sharply). Documents a concrete re-orientation of trade flows inside the triangle.
reports._notes: High-frequency quantitative marker of the triangle’s commercial rebalancing. Direct edge between the US-preferential and China-decoupling poles.
_referenced_by: Taiwan Customs trade statistics by partner

reports.title: Semiconductor supply-chain triad — design (US), manufacturing (Taiwan), residual materials / demand (China)
reports.publisher: Derived from MOEA, NSTC, US Commerce and industry statistics cited officially
reports.description: Structural description of the still-dominant pattern in which advanced design and EDA remain heavily US-centric, leading-edge manufacturing remains concentrated in Taiwan, and certain materials, mature-node capacity and end-demand retain significant Chinese weight. The triad is the industrial core of the larger economic-security triangle.
reports._cadence_original: continuous (via production, trade and investment series)
reports._notes: Industrial anatomy of the triangle. Makes the division of labour inside the semiconductor complex explicit for the force layout.
_referenced_by: US–Taiwan reshoring and investment MOU nodes

reports.title: Decoupling / friendshoring indicators (Taiwan outward investment and production relocation)
reports.publisher: Investment Commission / MOEA / survey-based and official relocation indicators
reports.description: Statistics and survey-derived indicators of Taiwanese firms reducing relative exposure to Mainland China and expanding capacity in the United States, Southeast Asia and other locations. Captures the operational side of diversification inside the triangle.
reports._notes: Dynamic process node. Links the stock of China exposure to the flow of new capacity toward the US and other partners.
_referenced_by: US-bound semiconductor investment and reshoring statistics
New Southbound Policy and Southeast Asian investment series

reports.title: Export-control and technology-security measures affecting the triangle
reports.publisher: US Commerce / Taiwan MOEA / related agencies
reports.description: Policy and statistical traces of US-led export controls on advanced semiconductors and manufacturing equipment, Taiwan’s alignment with those controls, and the resulting constraints on technology flows toward China. Forms the regulatory spine of the security side of the triangle.
reports._notes: Regulatory edge that actively shapes the triangle by limiting certain China-directed flows while deepening US–Taiwan technology alignment.
_referenced_by: Advanced-process capacity and equipment import statistics
Cross-strait technology and investment screening measures

reports.title: Residual cross-strait intermediate-goods and supply-chain linkages
reports.publisher: Customs / MAC / industry statistics
reports.description: Statistics on the remaining intermediate-goods trade and supply-chain connections between Taiwan and Mainland China, even as final-assembly and new investment have shifted. Documents the incomplete nature of decoupling inside the triangle.
reports._notes: Prevents the China pole from being treated as fully severed. Captures the sticky intermediate linkages that still exist.
_referenced_by: Cross-strait trade statistics and ECFA early-harvest data

reports.title: US–Taiwan security–economic nexus (arms sales + trade/investment instruments)
reports.publisher: Derived from FMS notifications, AIT–TECRO agreements, and Taiwan defence and trade statistics
reports.description: Relational node that binds the large and growing US arms-sales backlog to the parallel deepening of preferential trade, investment facilitation and supply-chain cooperation. Makes explicit that the security and economic tracks of the unofficial relationship reinforce each other inside the triangle.
reports._notes: Connects Batch 8 (economic-security) and Batch 9 (military) into a single US–Taiwan arm of the triangle.
_referenced_by: US–Taiwan ART, 21st-Century Trade Initiative and investment MOUs
National Defense Report and defence-budget series

reports.title: Triangle tension / risk indicators (official and statistical proxies)
reports.publisher: Derived from MAC, MND, CBC and related official releases
reports.description: Composite statistical and policy indicators that track rising or falling tension inside the triangle — changes in trade and investment shares, special defence budgets, export-control intensity, people-exchange volumes, and official risk language in the National Defense Report and MAC assessments.
reports._notes: Dynamic monitoring node. Gives the force layout a way to express intensity of competition and interdependence rather than static positions only.
_referenced_by: All major poles of the triangle (US economic-security, Chinese commercial, Taiwan semiconductor and defence)

reports.title: Semiconductor and high-tech talent / STEM workforce pipeline statistics
reports.publisher: National Science and Technology Council / Ministry of Education / industry-academia programmes / National Applied Research Laboratories (semiconductor center)
reports.description: Statistics and programme data on the supply of semiconductor and STEM talent — university and graduate output, industry-academia collaboration places, foreign student / work-study inflows into electronics manufacturing, and high-end R&D training capacity (e.g. National Semiconductor Center annual trainee volumes). Persistent shortages are a recurrent official and industry theme.
reports._notes: Critical constraint node. Tightens edges between the education, labour, R&D and semiconductor clusters and explains part of the wage premium and dual-structure pattern.
_referenced_by: R&D expenditure and science-park employment statistics
Industrial Innovation Act and talent-policy documents

reports.title: Dual-use and defense-relevant industrial statistics (shipbuilding, electronics, materials)
reports.publisher: Ministry of National Defense / Ministry of Economic Affairs / related industrial agencies
reports.description: Statistical and programme traces of industrial capacity that serves both commercial high-tech (especially electronics and advanced materials) and defence requirements (indigenous shipbuilding, missiles, C4ISR components). Captures the overlap zone between the semiconductor/electronics cluster and the defence-industrial cluster.
reports._notes: Explicit dual-use edge. Prevents the military and semiconductor clusters from remaining siloed.
_referenced_by: Indigenous naval shipbuilding and defence-industry statistics

reports.title: Taiwan cross-cluster densification meta-node (resilience–talent–energy–dual-use–fiscal)
reports.publisher: Derived from MND, NSTC, Energy Administration, MOF, MODA and related sources
reports.description: Meta-node that records the intentional densification of edges among previously somewhat separate clusters: whole-of-society resilience ↔ military, semiconductor talent ↔ industrial production & R&D, LNG/energy security ↔ ART commitments & AI electricity load, dual-use industry ↔ defence + electronics, fiscal revenue ↔ semiconductor profits & defence budgets. Serves as an explicit reminder to the force layout that these domains are now more densely interlinked.
reports._notes: Book-keeping and structural node. Helps the force mechanisms treat the newly strengthened cross-links as first-class rather than incidental.
_referenced_by: All detailed densification nodes in this batch
Earlier semiconductor, defence, energy, demographic and triangle meta-nodes

reports.title: Taiwan–Japan bilateral agreements and cooperation framework (fisheries, investment, customs, patent, etc.)
reports.publisher: Taiwan and Japan representative offices / related ministries
reports.description: Dense web of practical agreements covering fisheries, investment protection, customs mutual recognition, patent prosecution highway, product safety, search-and-rescue, environmental cooperation and numerous local-government twinning arrangements. Japan is both a technology partner and a security-adjacent neighbour.
reports._notes: High edge-density bilateral relationship that is often under-counted because it is not packaged as a single FTA. Explicitly raises the Japan pole of Taiwan’s external network.
_referenced_by: Trade and investment statistics with Japan
New Southbound and broader Indo-Pacific diversification

reports.title: New Southbound Policy — bilateral investment, trade-promotion and sectoral agreements
reports.publisher: Executive Yuan / Ministry of Economic Affairs / related agencies
reports.region: Taiwan–Southeast Asia / South Asia / Australia / New Zealand
reports.description: Growing set of investment-protection agreements, trade-promotion MOUs, and sectoral cooperation instruments (healthcare, agriculture, standards, etc.) concluded with Southbound partners. Complements the earlier New Southbound technology-diplomacy node with concrete legal and promotional instruments.
reports._notes: Legal-instrument densification of the Southbound diversification arm. Increases the number of discrete external nodes pulling on Taiwan.
_referenced_by: Outbound investment and trade statistics with ASEAN / India

reports.title: Taiwan as high-centrality economic-security hub (meta-node)
reports.publisher: Derived from trade, investment, semiconductor, defence and dialogue statistics
reports.description: Meta-node that records Taiwan’s unusually high top-level connectivity: simultaneous deep commercial residual with China, deepening economic-security and technology alignment with the United States, dense practical agreements with Japan and the EU, Southbound diversification instruments, and the global dependence on its advanced semiconductor capacity. Designed so the force layout can assign higher baseline degree / authority than a typical mid-sized economy.
reports._notes: Explicit structural claim that Taiwan is not a typical nation-node. Raises expected edge density at the top level of the graph.
_referenced_by: All major bilateral and plurilateral instruments (ART, ECFA, TID, Japan agreements, Southbound instruments)

reports.title: Social-structure consequences of semiconductor concentration (inequality, crowding-out, resource allocation)
reports.publisher: DGBAS / National Development Council / academic and official analyses citing official data
reports.description: Statistical and policy discussion of how the semiconductor boom concentrates wages, talent, capital, land and energy, producing measurable dualism: high earnings and job vacancies inside the electronics cluster alongside broader youth unemployment, skill mismatch, and crowding-out of non-semiconductor sectors. Official and quasi-official sources increasingly treat this as a structural social issue.
reports._cadence_original: continuous (via earnings, vacancy, education and NDC projections)
reports._notes: Direct social-structure edge from the industrial core. Answers the user’s observation that even Taiwan’s social structure is influenced by its hub role.
_referenced_by: Semiconductor talent pipeline and job-vacancy data

reports.title: Minilateral economic-security corridors involving Taiwan (e.g. Taiwan–Philippines Economic Corridor alignment with US–Japan–Philippines Luzon corridor)
reports.publisher: Taiwan and partner governments / related strategy documents
reports.description: Emerging minilateral arrangements that embed Taiwan’s semiconductor, smart-agriculture and technology investments inside broader US–Japan–partner economic-security corridors. Raises Taiwan’s connectivity beyond pure bilateral deals.
reports._notes: Higher-order external connectivity node. Moves Taiwan from bilateral spokes into minilateral webs.
_referenced_by: New Southbound Policy and Southbound agreements

reports.title: External regulatory and standards influence arising from Taiwan’s semiconductor position
reports.publisher: Derived from export-control alignment, industrial standards cooperation, and partner dialogues
reports.description: The set of export-control, investment-screening, standards and supply-chain-resilience rules that other jurisdictions adopt or coordinate in response to (or in concert with) Taiwan’s central manufacturing role. Taiwan is both a rule-taker (aligning with US controls) and a de-facto rule-shaper because its capacity forces partners to design policy around it.
reports._notes: Captures the ‘influences many’ side of the user’s hub observation — Taiwan’s position generates regulatory externalities for others.

reports.title: Taiwan hub → social-structure & policy-response meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from NDC, DGBAS, MOEA, MND and social-policy sources
reports.description: Meta-node that records the causal chain from Taiwan’s high-centrality semiconductor and economic-security role → concentrated wages, talent, capital and energy → measurable social dualism and crowding-out → policy responses in talent, family, fiscal redistribution and whole-of-society resilience. Makes the social-structure influence explicit for the force layout.
reports._notes: Closes the loop the user asked for: hub status is not only external; it reshapes internal social structure and therefore generates additional domestic policy nodes and edges.

reports.title: Administrative divisions of Taiwan — 6 special municipalities, 13 counties, 3 cities
reports.publisher: Ministry of the Interior / DGBAS
reports.description: The de-facto primary sub-national structure: six special municipalities (New Taipei, Taichung, Kaohsiung, Taipei, Taoyuan, Tainan), thirteen counties, and three provincial-level cities. Provinces are nominal; the 22 divisions are the operational units of local government and statistics.
reports._notes: Foundational spatial-structure node. Necessary before individual municipality or county nodes can be properly situated.
_referenced_by: Regional contrast and population concentration nodes

reports.title: Six special municipalities — population and economic concentration core
reports.publisher: DGBAS / Ministry of the Interior
reports.description: The six special municipalities (New Taipei, Taichung, Kaohsiung, Taipei, Taoyuan, Tainan) together contain roughly 70 % of Taiwan’s population and the large majority of high-value economic activity. They form the primary core of the spatial hierarchy.
reports._notes: Reinforces and expands the earlier regional-contrast node with explicit municipality-level framing.

reports.title: Taipei City — capital and financial/administrative centre
reports.publisher: Taipei City Government / DGBAS local indicators
reports.description: Capital special municipality. Highest population density, major financial and administrative functions, and consistently among the highest household disposable-income jurisdictions.
reports._notes: Primary administrative and financial municipal node.

reports.title: New Taipei City — largest-population special municipality
reports.publisher: New Taipei City Government / DGBAS
reports.description: Most populous special municipality (over 4 million). Functions as the broad residential and mixed industrial hinterland of the Taipei basin.
reports._notes: Population-weight municipal node.

reports.title: Taoyuan City — airport, logistics and northern industrial corridor
reports.publisher: Taoyuan City Government / related statistics
reports.description: Special municipality that contains Taiwan’s main international airport and significant industrial and logistics capacity linking the Taipei basin to the Hsinchu high-tech zone.
reports._notes: Gateway and industrial-corridor municipal node.
_referenced_by: Northern industrial corridor and science-park labour sheds

reports.title: Hsinchu City and Hsinchu County — highest-income high-tech cluster
reports.publisher: DGBAS local income statistics / Science Park administrations
reports.description: The Hsinchu area (city + county) consistently ranks at or near the top of household disposable-income rankings, driven by the Hsinchu Science Park and the surrounding semiconductor ecosystem. Distinct from the six special municipalities but central to the high-tech spatial structure.
reports._cadence_original: annual income rankings + continuous park statistics
reports._notes: Highest-income and purest high-tech geographic node. Critical for the dual-structure and social-impact stories.

reports.title: Taichung City — central Taiwan industrial and population centre
reports.publisher: Taichung City Government / DGBAS
reports.description: Second- or third-largest special municipality by population; major central industrial, commercial and residential hub. Contains the Central Taiwan Science Park.
reports._notes: Central Taiwan municipal anchor.

reports.title: Tainan City — southern historical and industrial centre
reports.publisher: Tainan City Government / related statistics
reports.description: Southern special municipality with historical significance and growing high-tech and industrial presence linked to the Southern Taiwan Science Park corridor.
reports._notes: Southern municipal node that participates in the semiconductor southward expansion.
_referenced_by: Southern Taiwan Science Park and S-corridor expansion

reports.title: Kaohsiung City — southern port, industrial and population centre
reports.publisher: Kaohsiung City Government / DGBAS
reports.description: Major southern special municipality, principal port, heavy-industrial base and significant population centre. Increasingly linked to the southern semiconductor and high-tech expansion.
reports._notes: Southern port and industrial municipal node.
_referenced_by: Southern Science Park and industrial expansion

reports.title: Eastern and peripheral counties — lower density, faster ageing
reports.publisher: DGBAS / Ministry of the Interior local statistics
reports.description: Counties such as Hualien, Taitung, Chiayi, Yunlin, Nantou and others that exhibit lower population density, higher ageing rates, and weaker high-tech presence. Form the primary periphery against the special-municipality and Hsinchu cores.
reports._notes: Periphery pole of the core–periphery spatial structure.

reports.title: Penghu County / Penghu Islands
reports.publisher: Penghu County Government / Ministry of the Interior
reports.description: Island county in the Taiwan Strait comprising the Penghu (Pescadores) archipelago. Distinct geographic, demographic and strategic profile from the main island.
reports._notes: Principal mid-Strait island group node.

reports.title: Kinmen County / Kinmen Islands
reports.publisher: Kinmen County Government / related agencies
reports.description: Island county lying immediately offshore from Xiamen (Fujian). Unique historical, demographic and cross-strait proximity profile; subject of distinct civil–military and exchange arrangements.
reports._notes: Most geopolitically exposed outlying-island node.

reports.title: Lienchiang County / Matsu Islands
reports.publisher: Lienchiang County Government / related agencies
reports.description: Northern outlying island group (Matsu) administered as Lienchiang County. Small population, strategic location, and distinct local statistics.
reports._notes: Northern outlying-island node.

reports.title: Outlying islands statistical and administrative set (Penghu, Kinmen, Matsu and related)
reports.publisher: Ministry of the Interior / local governments / MAC-related where relevant
reports.description: Collective statistical and administrative treatment of the major inhabited outlying island groups under ROC control. Distinct from the main island in demography, economy, defence posture and, in the cases of Kinmen and Matsu, cross-strait proximity.
reports._notes: Meta-node for the island geography that answers the user’s ‘bunch of islands’ question with statistical precision.
_referenced_by: Individual Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu nodes

reports.title: Northern high-tech corridor and southern S-corridor expansion
reports.publisher: Derived from science-park, industrial and municipal statistics
reports.description: Relational spatial node describing the traditional northern concentration (Taipei–Taoyuan–Hsinchu) and the deliberate southward expansion of semiconductor and high-tech capacity into the Tainan–Kaohsiung area (S-corridor).
reports._notes: Dynamic spatial edge that captures both historical concentration and policy-driven rebalancing.
_referenced_by: Science-park geography and Southern Science Park statistics
Municipal nodes along the western corridor
Industrial production and investment location analysis

reports.title: Taiwan sub-national spatial structure meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from MOI, DGBAS, NSTC and local government sources
reports.description: Meta-node that integrates the administrative division structure, six special municipalities, Hsinchu high-income cluster, eastern/peripheral counties, outlying island groups, science-park geography, local income rankings, and north–south corridor dynamics into a coherent sub-national layer. Raises the internal spatial edge density of the Taiwan hub.
reports._notes: Integrating node so the force layout treats Taiwan’s internal geography as a dense, multi-polar structure rather than a single national point.
_referenced_by: All detailed municipal, county, island and science-park nodes in this batch

reports.title: Semiconductor ‘five shortages’ framing (water, power, labour, land, talent)
reports.publisher: Industry and government sources (recurrent in official speeches and policy documents)
reports.description: Recurring policy and industry framing of the five binding constraints on semiconductor expansion: water, electric power, labour, land and high-end talent. Functions as a conceptual but heavily cited organising node that pulls together previously separate resource, labour and land series.
reports._notes: High-citation organising node. Explicitly densifies edges among the resource, labour and industrial clusters.
_referenced_by: Water, energy, talent, labour-shortage and science-park land statistics
Industrial Innovation Act and capacity-expansion planning

reports.title: Taiwan continued-dig densification meta-node (indigenous, foreign-resident geography, water/resource constraints)
reports.publisher: Derived from MOI, CIP, Immigration Agency, Water Resources Agency and related sources
reports.description: Meta-node recording the further densification of social (Indigenous population and geography, foreign-resident distribution) and resource (water, drought, industrial-water, land, five-shortages) layers and their edges into the demographic, spatial, semiconductor and resilience clusters.
reports._notes: Book-keeping node for the continued dig.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Earlier demographic, sub-national, semiconductor and resilience meta-nodes

reports.title: Dual-use and defence-industrial location patterns (science parks, shipyards, southern corridor)
reports.publisher: Derived from MND, MOEA, NSTC and local industrial statistics
reports.region: Especially western and southern industrial zones
reports.description: Spatial patterning of dual-use and defence-relevant capacity: concentration of advanced electronics and materials in science parks (Hsinchu core and southern expansion), naval shipbuilding and related yards, and the co-location pressures that arise when commercial high-tech and defence requirements share the same constrained land, water and talent pools.
reports._notes: More precise spatial densification of the dual-use edge requested by the user.
_referenced_by: Indigenous naval shipbuilding and defence-industry nodes

reports.title: Environmental–cultural–local-fiscal densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from MOENV, language councils, MOF and related sources
reports.description: Meta-node that records the further densification of environmental quality (air, local gradients), cultural/language (use statistics, Hakka and national-languages frameworks, institutional budgets), local fiscal capacity (taxable income and government finance by division), and more precise dual-use location patterns, together with their edges into the spatial, semiconductor, social and resilience clusters.
reports._notes: Book-keeping node for this multi-domain dig.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Earlier sub-national, environmental, social-structure and dual-use nodes

reports.title: Regional contrast — Special Municipalities vs counties / population and economic concentration
reports.publisher: DGBAS / Ministry of the Interior / local governments
reports.description: Statistical framework highlighting the extreme concentration of population and economic activity in the six special municipalities (Taipei, New Taipei, Taoyuan, Taichung, Tainan, Kaohsiung), which together account for roughly 70 % of the population, versus more rapidly ageing and lower-density counties (especially eastern and agricultural counties).
reports._notes: Spatial hierarchy node. Parallel to Seoul Capital Area and Tokyo/Okinawa contrasts. Essential for force-layout geographic clustering and for capturing core–periphery differentials.
_referenced_by: Population and vital statistics by locality

reports.title: Taipei–Hsinchu high-tech / administrative axis statistics
reports.publisher: DGBAS / Science Park administrations / local statistical offices
reports.description: Combined statistical view of Taipei (administrative and financial centre) and Hsinchu (science-park / semiconductor heartland) as the primary high-value axis of the Taiwanese economy.
reports._notes: Focused regional node that tightens the link between administrative capital and the foundry cluster.

reports.title: Advanced-process and packaging capacity indicators (official and industry-linked)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Economic Affairs / NSTC / industry associations cited in official releases
reports.description: Indicators and official commentary on leading-edge process nodes (5 nm, 3 nm, 2 nm) and advanced packaging capacity concentrated in Taiwan. While firm-level data are private, the statistical and policy literature continuously references Taiwan’s dominant global share of advanced capacity.
reports._notes: Strategic capacity node. Taiwan’s overwhelming share of the most advanced foundry and packaging capacity is the structural reason the semiconductor cluster carries such high authority in any global or regional graph.
_referenced_by: Electronic components production and science-park IC revenue

reports.title: Taiwan semiconductor / electronics cluster — overview meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from MOEA, NSTC, DGBAS and CBC sources
reports.description: Meta-node that situates the electronic-components production series, computers/optical production, science-park revenue, Industrial Innovation Act incentives, semiconductor trade, employment and advanced-capacity indicators as a single coherent high-authority industrial complex.
reports._notes: Explicit cluster-level node so the force layout can treat the entire semiconductor complex as a tightly bound, high-mass object rather than a collection of weakly linked leaves. This is the structural feature the user requested to be ‘well fleshed out’.
_referenced_by: All detailed semiconductor and electronics nodes listed above
National accounts, BOP, R&D and regional statistics that treat electronics as the leading sector

reports.title: Taiwanese semiconductor investment and capacity expansion in the United States (official and reported figures)
reports.publisher: MOEA / Investment Commission / US Commerce / industry reporting cited in official releases
reports.description: Statistics and official commitments concerning Taiwanese semiconductor firms’ direct investment and capacity build-out in the United States (fabs, packaging, materials, equipment ecosystem). Figures in the hundreds of billions have been associated with the recent AIT–TECRO investment understandings.
reports._notes: Quantifies the physical manifestation of the economic-security partnership. Creates concrete edges from the domestic semiconductor cluster into the US–Taiwan architecture and into global supply-chain resilience analysis.
_referenced_by: AIT–TECRO investment MOU and ART fact sheets
Science-park and advanced-process capacity indicators (outbound side)
reports._not_a_publication_reason: Grok, agreeing with Claude: no discrete official statistical product; the figures come from company announcements and ad-hoc briefings.

reports.title: Taiwan semiconductor–economic-security–sovereignty architecture (meta-node)
reports.publisher: Derived from AIT–TECRO instruments, MOEA, NSTC and CBC sources
reports.description: Meta-node that binds the domestic semiconductor manufacturing cluster (production, science parks, advanced capacity, trade) to the international instruments that protect and expand Taiwan’s economic security and de-facto international space (ART, 21st-Century Trade Initiative, investment MOUs, TIFA, export-control alignment, New Southbound technology diplomacy).
reports._notes: Highest-level integrating node for the user’s requested theme. Allows the force layout to treat ‘chips + the deals that protect the chip island’ as a single high-mass, geopolitically charged object rather than disconnected commercial and diplomatic leaves.
_referenced_by: All detailed semiconductor and US–Taiwan economic-security nodes in Batches 7 and 8
Cross-strait statistics and ECFA (as the contrasting relationship)
National accounts, BOP and R&D series that treat electronics as the strategic sector

reports.title: Coast Guard–Navy wartime linkage statistics (Anping-class / missile stockpiles)
reports.publisher: Coast Guard Administration / Navy / MND
reports.description: Statistical and programme information on the dual-use Anping-class patrol vessels (based on the Tuo Chiang design) and the Navy’s stockpiling of Hsiung Feng anti-ship missiles for wartime fit-out of Coast Guard hulls. Illustrates the grey-zone to high-intensity continuum in maritime force structure.
reports._notes: Distinctive Taiwan feature: Coast Guard hulls designed for rapid wartime conversion. Strengthens the navy–asymmetric cluster.
_referenced_by: Defence budget and munitions stockpile lines
Maritime domain awareness and grey-zone analysis

reports.title: Taiwan military–navy–defence-industrial cluster (meta-node)
reports.publisher: Derived from MND, Navy, Coast Guard, US FMS and SIPRI sources
reports.description: Meta-node that binds defence budget, National Defense Report, indigenous naval shipbuilding, Coast Guard–Navy linkage, US arms-sales backlog, domestic defence industry, asymmetric special budgets, manpower and arms-transfer statistics into a coherent security cluster that sits alongside the semiconductor and US–Taiwan economic-security architecture.
reports._notes: Integrating node so the force layout can treat the military/navy complex as a high-mass object that interacts with both the chip-sovereignty architecture and the broader demographic and fiscal clusters.
_referenced_by: All detailed military and navy nodes in this batch
US–Taiwan ART / investment MOU / economic-security nodes (Batch 8)
Semiconductor and dual-use technology nodes where relevant

findings.title: Coast Guard–Navy wartime linkage statistics (Anping-class / missile stockpiles)
findings.finding: Still not found, and this is not a publication. The specific thing the node describes - a Coast Guard-Navy wartime linkage, i.e. Anping-class hulls fitted out with Navy Hsiung Feng missiles held in stockpile - is an analytic construct assembled from procurement records and commentary, not an official series or single official document. The Anping-class programme itself is covered by Ocean Affairs Council / Coast Guard Administration news items (e.g. the naming and launch of the twelfth and final hull, Donggang), but the OAC news URL I identified returned a 404 page when fetched, and in any case a launch announcement is not the 'wartime linkage statistics' the node asks for. Missile stockpile figures are not published. Recording null.
